title: A friend from your childhood
bullets: where and how you met each other
and explain what made you like him/her

notes.label: Met
notes.text: alley in Đống Đa, age 5; knocked on our door

notes.label: Together
notes.text: alley football, paper boats, kites on the dyke, dried squid

notes.label: Why liked
notes.text: fearless, loyal, funny; reconnected on Facebook

segments.v: I want to talk about my childhood friend Bin. We met when I was five. He lived near my house in a small alley in Đống Đa. One day he came to my house and asked me to play football. After that, we became best friends. We often played football in the alley. We also played with paper boats when it rained and flew kites in the summer. We shared snacks and secrets. I liked him because he was brave and funny. He always helped me when older children teased me. When I was eleven, my family moved to Cầu Giấy and later his family moved to Hồ Chí Minh City. We didn't talk for a long time, but last year we found each other on Facebook. Now we still keep in touch.

fluency.band9: Nickname → how they met (vivid) → activities (three scenes) → why liked (what-clause) → separation → reconnection → future.

grammar.band9: Relative clause with “where”, “would” in a relative clause for typical behaviour (the kind of kid who'd climb any tree), a what-clause (What made me like him so much was…), and present perfect (We've promised to meet up…).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 is clear and in order. Band 9 opens with a cultural detail, uses vivid childhood images, explains why the speaker liked him with “What made me like him… was…”, and brings the story to the present.
